title: Quetzalcoatl: Departure from Tollan
subtitle: A Toltec episode as transmitted by Spence

departure.author: Lewis Spence
departure.locator: Chapter II · MEXICAN MYTHOLOGY; Chapter II · MEXICAN MYTHOLOGY, normalized characters 20022-20201
departure.excerpt: On reaching the summit of Mount Poyauhtecatl he slid to the base. Arriving at the sea-shore, he embarked upon a raft of serpents, and was wafted away toward the land of Tlapallan.
departure.note: Verbatim prose from Lewis Spence's early twentieth-century synthesis, not a direct translation of the Indigenous source material he discusses. Preserve its dated, colonial framing.

narrativeBlocks.title: The feathered serpent as king
narrativeBlocks.body: In one strand of the tradition, Quetzalcoatl — the Feathered Serpent — was the priest-king of the Toltec city of Tollan: a wise ruler who taught crafts and opposed human sacrifice.

narrativeBlocks.title: Tricked by the sorcerer
narrativeBlocks.body: The dark sorcerer Tezcatlipoca, his rival, tricks him into drunkenness and shame — the disgraced king can no longer hold his city.

narrativeBlocks.title: The raft of serpents
narrativeBlocks.body: At the eastern shore he departs on a raft of serpents, promising to return — the famous eastward exit into myth.

narrativeBlocks.title: The myth that met the sea
narrativeBlocks.body: Centuries later the story would be told of the Mexica looking east for a returning god when strangers landed — one of history's most contested claims.

narrativeBlocks.title: A Toltec inheritance
narrativeBlocks.body: The tale reached the Mexica through Toltec prestige — one people's god-king became another's omen, and the line between legend and later propaganda stays blurry.
